observation_summary: The MonthDay class fails to perform arithmetic operations (plus/minus months/days) when the instance is set to February 29th. It throws an IllegalFieldValueException because it attempts to validate the day-of-month against a range [1, 28] while the date is still conceptually February 29th.
hypothesis: The logic in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add() incorrectly attempts to validate the day-of-month field against the bounds of a non-leap year before the full arithmetic operation is completed. The algorithm needs to handle the leap day (February 29th) as a valid state during intermediate calculations for MonthDay objects.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add() to bypass or adjust the strict validation of the day-of-month field when performing arithmetic on MonthDay objects, allowing the leap day to persist or be handled correctly during the transition.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points directly to BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add() calling FieldUtils.verifyValueBounds, which triggers the exception. Since the operation is valid for a MonthDay (which represents a recurring date), the algorithm's assumption that it must validate against a standard year's bounds is the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic flaw in how the library handles date arithmetic for partial dates (MonthDay). It is not a missing check (the check exists but is applied incorrectly), nor is it a simple initialization error. The procedure for adding/subtracting months/days is fundamentally flawed for the specific case of leap days in a partial date context.
evidence_used: org.joda.time.IllegalFieldValueException: Value 29 for dayOfMonth must be in the range [1,28]

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the failure manifests as a failed check, the root cause is the algorithmic design of the add() method, which incorrectly enforces standard year bounds on a partial date that is allowed to be a leap day.
